findings.what: The scoped S1 checks don't prove 'only from the app subnet and agent range, denies the rest'. A second Allow rule, or an extra source in the existing allow, still passes
findings.why: Line 171 claims more than lines 200-212 prove. The allow check is satisfied if any one 1433 rule has both prefixes (substring `in`). Nothing rejects other Allow rules or extra sources. Mutant 1: add 'allow-sql-any' (Inbound, Allow, Tcp, sourceAddressPrefix '*', 1433, priority 200) to privateEndpointNsg. allows=[100,200], deny=4000, so every check passes, yet 1433 is open to the whole VNet and peers, which is the S1 exposure. Mutant 2: sourceAddressPrefixes [appIntegrationPrefix, agentAddressPrefix, 'VirtualNetwork'] also passes. Mutant 3: an Allow on port '*' isn't in `allows`, so it isn't checked at all. The deny check also ignores protocol and destinationAddressPrefix. The infrastructure at HEAD is correct (one allow with exactly two sources, then deny-all at 4000). The gap is only in the oracle. This is the same class as A2.2 R1 but a different mutant, and 781815a didn't close it. Per David's instruction for this round, this P2 is carried with no further fix round.
